definition: The market value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country during a period (a year or quarter). In India's national accounts GDP is derived as GVA at basic prices plus net taxes on products.
formula: GDP = GVA at basic prices + Product taxes - Product subsidies
note: Measured both at current prices (nominal) and constant prices (real, at base-year prices).

definition: The value of output less the value of intermediate consumption. It measures the contribution of each producer, industry or sector to the economy. MoSPI reports GVA at basic prices by industry.
formula: GVA = Value of output - Intermediate consumption

definition: GVA valued at basic prices, i.e. the amount receivable by the producer excluding taxes on products and including subsidies on products. It includes production taxes less production subsidies.
formula: GVA at basic prices = CE + OS/MI + CFC + Production taxes - Production subsidies

definition: GVA valued at the cost of factors of production (labour, capital). It excludes all taxes on production and products and includes subsidies. Used as the headline measure in India before the 2011-12 base revision.
formula: GVA at factor cost = GVA at basic prices - (Production taxes - Production subsidies)

definition: Taxes payable per unit of a good or service (GST, excise duty, customs duty, etc.) minus subsidies payable per unit (food, fertiliser, petroleum subsidies, etc.). Bridges GVA at basic prices and GDP.
formula: Net taxes on products = Product taxes - Product subsidies

definition: Taxes and subsidies on production that are not levied per unit of output, e.g. land revenue, stamp and registration fees, professional tax, and subsidies to railways or village and small industries.
GDP less consumption of fixed capital (depreciation). It represents domestic production net of the capital used up in producing it.
The decline in the current value of the stock of fixed assets owned and used by producers as a result of physical deterioration, normal obsolescence or accidental damage during the period.
GDP plus net primary income (compensation of employees and property and entrepreneurial income) receivable from the rest of the world.
formula: GNI = GDP + Net primary income from abroad

definition: GNI less consumption of fixed capital. NNI at current prices is commonly referred to as 'national income'.
Net national income divided by the mid-year population. The standard measure of average income per person used in Indian official statistics.
formula: Per capita NNI = NNI / Mid-year population

definition: GNI plus net other current transfers (e.g. remittances, grants) received from the rest of the world. It is the income available for final consumption and saving.
formula: GNDI = GNI + Net other current transfers from abroad

term: Primary Income Receivable (Net) from Rest of the World
definition: Compensation of employees and property income (interest, dividends, profits) received from non-residents less the same paid to non-residents.
Expenditure incurred by resident households and non-profit institutions serving households (NPISH) on final consumption goods and services, whether in the domestic market or abroad.
Current expenditure of general government (Centre, States, local bodies) on compensation of employees and purchase of goods and services, net of sales, for collective and individual consumption.

Acquisitions less disposals of produced fixed assets (buildings, machinery, equipment, intellectual property products, cultivated biological resources) by resident producers during the period. The main measure of investment.
The value of entries into inventories (raw materials, work in progress, finished goods) less the value of withdrawals and recurrent losses during the period.
Produced goods of considerable value acquired primarily as stores of value rather than for production or consumption, e.g. precious metals, gems, jewellery and works of art.
The total of gross fixed capital formation, changes in stocks and acquisitions less disposals of valuables. In the industry-of-use presentation it is also shown by the industry that uses the assets.
formula: GCF = GFCF + Change in stocks + Valuables

term: Exports and Imports of Goods and Services
definition: Transactions in goods and services (sales, barter, gifts) between residents and non-residents. Net exports (X - M) enter the expenditure-side GDP.

The difference between GDP estimated from the production side and the sum of expenditure components (PFCE + GFCE + GCF + net exports). Shown as a separate line because the two approaches use independent data sources.
formula: Discrepancy = GDP - (PFCE + GFCE + GCF + X - M)

definition: Gross national disposable income less final consumption expenditure. Reported by institutional sector: households, non-financial corporations, financial corporations and general government.
Gross saving and gross capital formation expressed as a percentage of GNDI or GDP respectively at current prices.
Values measured at the prices prevailing in the year of reference. Growth at current prices combines volume growth and price change.
Values measured at the prices of a fixed base year, so that growth reflects changes in volume (quantity) only. Real GDP growth is the headline growth rate.

The reference year whose prices are used to value constant-price estimates and whose economic structure (weights, data sources, methods) anchors the series. India's series have used bases 2004-05, 2011-12 and 2022-23. Series with different base years are not directly comparable.
Estimates for years before the base year compiled to be comparable with the current base-year series (e.g. 2011-12 base estimates for 2004-05 to 2010-11).
The ratio of an aggregate at current prices to the same aggregate at constant prices, times 100. The GDP deflator is an economy-wide measure of inflation.
Percentage change over the same period of the previous year. For quarterly GDP, growth is year-on-year (Q over the same quarter of the previous year), not seasonally adjusted quarter-on-quarter.
India's fiscal year from 1 April to 31 March, written e.g. 2024-25. Q1 = Apr-Jun, Q2 = Jul-Sep, Q3 = Oct-Dec, Q4 = Jan-Mar.
The first estimate of annual GDP for the current financial year, released in early January, based on partial-year indicators; used for Union Budget preparation.
Revised annual estimate for the current financial year released at the end of February together with the Q3 quarterly estimates.
Annual estimate for the just-completed financial year released at the end of May together with the Q4 quarterly estimates.

Successive revisions of an annual estimate as fuller data (e.g. ASI, budget documents, enterprise filings) becomes available, generally released at the end of February in the following years. The Third Revised Estimate is treated as final.
Estimates of GDP and GVA for each quarter, released about two months after the quarter ends (end of February, May, August and November).
Total remuneration in cash or kind payable by an employer to an employee for work done, including employers' contributions to social security.

The surplus from production after paying compensation of employees and production taxes. For unincorporated household enterprises, where owner's labour and capital returns cannot be separated, it is called mixed income.

Groups of resident units with similar economic behaviour: non-financial corporations (public and private), financial corporations, general government, households (including unincorporated enterprises) and NPISH.

GVA is classified by industry following the National Industrial Classification: agriculture, forestry & fishing; mining & quarrying; manufacturing; electricity, gas, water & utilities; construction; trade, hotels, transport, communication & broadcasting; financial, real estate & professional services; public administration, defence & other services.

Primary: agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining. Secondary: manufacturing, electricity/gas/water, construction. Tertiary (services): trade, transport, communication, finance, real estate, public administration and other services.

The state-level counterpart of GDP: value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of a state. Compiled by State Directorates of Economics & Statistics and published by MoSPI.

term: Net State Domestic Product / Per Capita NSDP
definition: GSDP less consumption of fixed capital. Per capita NSDP divides NSDP by the state's population and is the usual measure of state per capita income.
The international statistical standard for national accounts adopted by the UN Statistical Commission (SNA 2008; SNA 2025 being the latest update). India's national accounts broadly follow SNA 2008.

Matrices showing how supplies of products from domestic industries and imports are used for intermediate consumption, final consumption, capital formation and exports. Used to reconcile production and expenditure estimates.
The statistical wing of MoSPI (formed by merging CSO and NSSO) responsible for compiling and releasing national accounts estimates.
